method: 15-agent workflow: 6 web sweeps -> synthesis -> 8 blind refuters (claim-only, refute-default). 40 raw findings; 8/8 recommendations survived; 0 killed.

survived.title: Re-grade the 2019-2024 walk at real historical entry prices (Odds API snapshots + free SBR open/close archive) before trusting any doctrine
survived.claim: The flagship doctrine signals (+20% underdog ATS ROI, rest sweet spot, weather buckets) were measured against ~closing nflverse lines and are therefore contaminated by closing-line lookahead; nfelo's public 17-season backtest quantifies the damage at roughly 3.6pp ATS (56.78% vs opening lines collapsing to 53.13% vs close). Re-grading against timestamped pre-close prices converts the admitted 'optimistic upper bound' into an honest entry-price backtest and tells you which doctrine survives.
survived.evidence: The Odds API historical endpoint serves 5-minute odds snapshots (featured markets from Jun 2020, player props from May 2023) via a date parameter, so 2023-2024 walk weeks and ALL prop weeks can be re-graded at T-minus-X-hours prices. For 2019-2021, the MIT-licensed FinnedAI/sportsbookreview-scraper mirror ships nfl_archive_10Y.json with verified per-game open AND close spreads/totals/ML — enabling both 'bet at open, judge at close' pseudo-CLV grading and an open-to-close drift feature that discriminates real dog edge from steam-side artifact. nfelo's open-vs-close gap is the concrete prior for how much measured ROI will evaporate.
survived.first_step: Download nfl_archive_10Y.json from the FinnedAI repo, join to the 2019-2021 walk weeks on date+teams, and re-grade the underdog-ATS doctrine twice: at opening lines and at closing lines. If the +20% ROI does not survive at open (or concentrates on dogs the market moved AWAY from), demote it before the 8/17 2025-holdout validation.

verdict.reasoning: Attempted refutation failed on every checkable pillar. (1) The nfelo citation verifies exactly: nfeloapp.com's public model-performance page reports 56.78% ATS vs opening lines and 53.13% vs closing lines over a 17-season backtest (2009-2025) — the ~3.6pp open-vs-close gap is real and current, demonstrating that the choice of reference line is first-order for measured ATS performance. (2) Data feasibility holds: The Odds API historical snapshots begin June 6, 2020 (10-min intervals; 5-min from Sept 2022), so they cannot cover 2019 alone — but the claim explicitly pairs them with the free SBR archive (sportsbookreviewsonline.com), which does provide downloadable Excel files of opening AND closing spreads/totals/moneylines for NFL seasons including 2019, so the 2019-2024 re-grade is executable as described. (3) The methodological premise is standard quant hygiene: consensus closing lines (nflverse-style) are the sharpest, non-timestamped, non-executable-all-week prices; signals whose selection criteria are defined by the closing number (e.g., 'underdog' status set by close) embed outcome-correlated late information relative to any earlier entry, and a +20% underdog ATS ROI (~63% win rate needed at -110) is far outside anything in published literature (~52-54% for the best-known situational angles), which independently supports treating the current grading as untrustworthy until re-graded at entry prices. One caveat that does NOT rise to refutation: the nfelo gap's direction shows close-grading can also UNDERSTATE a sharp model (nfelo does better vs open), so '3.6pp' is best read as the magnitude of reference-line sensitivity rather than a guaranteed inflation of these specific doctrine signals — but the claim's operative recommendation ('re-grade at timestamped pre-close prices and see which doctrine survives') is robust to that direction uncertainty and is the correct procedure either way. Sources: https://www.nfeloapp.com/games/nfl-model-performance/ ; https://the-odds-api.com/historical-odds-data/ ; https://sportsbookreviewsonline.com/scoresoddsarchives/nfl/nfloddsarchives.htm

survived.title: Make the receipts-page CLV metric devig-correct, Pinnacle-benchmarked, and market-scoped (no CLV verdicts on props)
survived.claim: Three mechanical fixes to the planned CLV-beat-rate metric: (1) compute CLV against the VIG-FREE close — raw line-vs-line CLV overstates edge 3-4x (worked example: -195 entry vs -220 close looks like ~4% CLV, is <1% devigged); (2) pin the closing benchmark to Pinnacle (or Circa/BookMaker fallback), never a consensus average; (3) grade props by realized results with binomial CIs, not CLV, because low-limit prop closes are not efficient prices. Without these, a raw beat rate can clear the pre-registered 55% threshold while the devigged rate sits at ~50% (no edge).
survived.evidence: Buchdahl's 136,876-match Pinnacle dataset shows devigged sharp closes predict realized returns almost exactly 1:1 (gradient ~1, high R^2), while the same exercise using four soft books' devigged closes as fair value predicts nothing — benchmark choice is load-bearing, and blending soft closes into a consensus destroys the metric. Unabated (professional-bettor consensus) states flatly that CLV is meaningless in props and gives the verifiable devig arithmetic. The Sports Trading Network 3,000-pick sample (+8.9% realized at -0.2% expected-by-CLV) shows orthogonal-information edges can flunk CLV, so keep a dual ledger (devigged CLV AND realized ROI) and only kill an angle when both are negative.
survived.first_step: In the receipts-page grader, store the full two-sided closing prices plus the benchmark book name for every bet, add a devig step (reuse the CLV-pivot machinery) before computing beat rate, and split the verdict metric: devigged CLV beat rate for spreads/totals, realized ROI + binomial CI for props. Publish both raw and devigged numbers for auditability.

verdict.reasoning: Attempted refutation failed on all three legs. (1) Devig: independent math check confirms the worked example — -195 entry vs -220 close is +4.0% raw CLV (1.5128/1.4545) but only ~+0.75% against the devigged fair close (~-199, from a typical 30-cent line), matching Unabated's published example almost exactly; multiple independent sources (Unabated, thecapper.io, dratings, gamblingnerd) instruct computing CLV against the no-vig close and warn raw CLV inflates edge by roughly the hold (~4.5%). The "3-4x overstatement" is representative, even conservative for this example (~5x), and a raw beat rate clearing 55% while the devigged rate sits near 50% follows mechanically from that padding. (2) Pinnacle as the closing benchmark is the documented industry standard (Buchdahl's CLV research, multiple CLV trackers), with Circa/BookMaker the recognized US sharp fallbacks; vigged consensus averages are explicitly discouraged. (3) Props: direct expert consensus surfaced ("CLV doesn't mean anything in props — very few market-making books"); low-limit prop closes ride thin action and diverge for risk-tolerance reasons, so grading props by realized results with binomial CIs is the sound alternative. No credible counter-evidence found; the claim is standard sharp-betting methodology, correctly stated.

survived.title: Add a deterministic shrinkage gate on every doctrine lesson and keep bet sizing out of the LLM: Beta(50,50) posterior + fractional Kelly + beta calibration
survived.claim: Every distilled lesson is 'this bucket went x wins in n bets' — exactly the setup where raw win rates overstate. Gate: a lesson feeds forward only if its Beta(50,50) posterior mean win rate (x+50)/(n+100) clears breakeven (52.4% at -110); this one line kills small-n mirages deterministically and the LLM cannot tune it. Stake paper bets at k*Kelly with k≈0.25-0.5 computed in code from calibrated probabilities, never by the model. Recalibrate confidences with beta calibration (not Platt or isotonic), which is stable at the ~100-200 graded picks per bucket the loop actually produces.
survived.evidence: Chu, Wu & Swartz derive the closed-form modified Kelly and show 65% vs 53% profitable-season rates and ~0% vs ~38% ruin-halving vs raw Kelly in simulation (with published R code); Baker & McHale/Downey quantify that drawdown control, not uncertainty per se, justifies k≈0.25-0.5 (10th-percentile optimization cuts 0.40→0.28, and 0.13→0.05 for longshot-shaped bets like props). The live 7-LLM betting benchmark found the winning behavior was explicit Kelly/EV math, not deeper narrative analysis — Gemini bet $982 of $1,000 on day one — so staking must be code. Metricgate's comparison gives the sample-size thresholds: Platt ~50 but distorts calibrated regions, isotonic needs 500-1,000+, beta calibration works from ~100-200 and can represent the identity map, making it safe on the already-tight 0.5-0.7 band.
survived.first_step: Add the one-line Beta(50,50) posterior check to the doctrine-distillation step (reject any lesson whose posterior mean <= 0.524), then fit a beta calibration map (logistic regression on [ln s, ln(1-s)]) on the walk's graded picks, refit per walk-forward step.

verdict.reasoning: Attempted refutation failed on every checkable component. (1) Breakeven math is correct: -110 implies 110/210 = 52.38%. (2) The Beta(50,50) gate was verified computationally: impossible to pass below n=6, requires 8/10, 13/20, 29/50 wins, and a null p=0.5 bucket passes at n=8 with only ~3.5% probability — it genuinely and deterministically suppresses small-n mirages, and being one line of arithmetic it is untunable by the LLM; prior mean 50% < breakeven means zero-evidence lessons are blocked by default. (3) Fractional Kelly at k≈0.25-0.5 computed in code is the documented professional standard against estimation error (overbetting asymmetrically worse; half Kelly ≈75% growth at ~half variance; quarter Kelly the most-cited professional fraction). (4) Beta calibration (Kull/Silva Filho/Flach 2017) is independently documented as the right choice at ~100-200 samples: isotonic overfits small calibration sets (guidance: needs ≫1000), Platt assumes the wrong distortion for extreme-scored [0,1] outputs and can uncalibrate a calibrated model since its family excludes the identity, while beta calibration is a stable 3-parameter map designed for [0,1] scores that includes the identity. Residual quibbles (arbitrary prior strength, posterior mean vs lower credible bound, multiplicity across buckets at ~3.5% null pass rate) do not contradict the claim as stated. The claim is technically sound and independently supported.

survived.title: Feed Sonnet pre-aggregated EPA features (the validated 8-feature EWMA recipe), never raw stats — and benchmark against nfelo's numbers
survived.claim: Compute the Open Source Football 8-feature set per matchup — EWMA passing-offense/passing-defense/rushing-offense/rushing-defense EPA per play for each team, dynamic 10-20 game windows weighted by play count — and inject them as small labeled scalars into the weekly prompt. Never hand the model raw play-by-play or long tables: LLMs measurably fail at numeric fusion across game narratives. Two pre-tested pitfalls to skip: opponent-adjusting defensive EPA slightly HURTS, and weight by plays not games.
survived.evidence: The OSF two-part study (reproducible, nflfastR data, 10-fold CV on 1999-2019) validated exactly this feature construction at 63.5% SU accuracy and showed passing EPA dominates via SHAP-style importance. SportsMetrics (arXiv 2402.10979) benchmarked GPT-4-class models on NBA/NFL play-by-play and found material failures in tracking/cross-referencing numbers — aggregation is not a language task, which is also why the loop's doctrine distillation works better than its per-game number crunching. nfelo's public table (56.78% ATS vs open, 53.13% vs close, 3.75% avg CLV, built on the same nflverse data) supplies the concrete bars the loop and the receipts page should be measured against, and its 'smart market reversion' (shrink model spread toward the posted line) is a copyable technique for the quant fair-value model.
survived.first_step: Port the OSF feature script (published R, trivial to translate) to compute the 8 EPA features from the nflverse pbp already in the stack, serve them for weeks < N in the walk, and A/B one replayed season with vs without the features in Sonnet's context against the frozen graded record.

verdict.reasoning:
I attempted to refute the claim and could not — nearly every component checks out against independent sources.

1) The "Open Source Football 8-feature EWMA recipe" is real and accurately described. The OSF post "Exploring Rolling Averages of EPA" (Jack Lichtenstein, Dec 2020, opensourcefootball.com/posts/2020-12-29-exploring-rolling-averages-of-epa/) computes exactly passing-offense, passing-defense, rushing-offense, rushing-defense EPA/play per team (4 features x 2 teams = 8 per matchup), finds a DYNAMIC window ("a ten game window to predict the winner of the 11th game... for the 15th game, a 14 game window", extending to ~20 for Super Bowl teams) beats a static 10-game window, and weights "EPA by the number of plays in each game of the window" rather than equally by game. Both pre-tested pitfalls are verbatim-accurate: the article states "adjusting defensive EPA/play for opponent offenses faced actually decreases its predictive power, albeit a very small amount," and play-weighting outperformed game-weighting.

2) The nfelo benchmark is applicable: nfelo publishes a "Weighted EPA Methodology & Performance" page (nfeloapp.com) built on the same weighted-EPA family, so benchmarking the 8-feature outputs against nfelo's published numbers is a coherent, available frozen anchor.

3) The LLM sub-claim ("never hand the model raw play-by-play or long tables; LLMs measurably fail at numeric fusion") is independently supported by benchmark literature: table-reasoning benchmarks (TReB, TabularMath) show aggregation/comparison across many values is a key bottleneck with top scores ~60; "Why Large Language Models Fail at Tabular Prediction" (arXiv 2608.02412) shows the LLM is the only method of nine whose performance degrades as features are added even with information content held fixed; numeracy benchmarks confirm degradation on long contexts and multi-value aggregation. Pre-aggregating into small labeled scalars is the standard mitigation.

Only caveat found: the OSF article's best-performing mix used EWMA for offensive EPA but running/simple averages for some rushing and defensive measures, so "EWMA for all 8" slightly oversimplifies the optimal variant — a nuance, not a refutation. The recipe is from 2020 but remains the reference public approach (nfelo still runs weighted EPA); it is a feature-engineering claim, not a market-edge claim, so "arbed away" does not apply.

Sources: https://opensourcefootball.com/posts/2020-12-29-exploring-rolling-averages-of-epa/ , https://opensourcefootball.com/posts/2020-08-20-adjusting-epa-for-strenght-of-opponent/ , https://www.nfeloapp.com/analysis/weighted-EPA-methodology-and-performance/ , https://arxiv.org/html/2608.02412 , https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.18421

survived.title: Harvest CLV with entry-timing rules: bet against the most recent line move, log originator-vs-follower lag, and act in QB-news repricing windows
survived.claim: Since CLV beat rate is THE public metric, timing is a first-order lever independent of pick quality: (1) NFL pre-game price changes 2019-2023 are negatively autocorrelated (books overreact), so entering AGAINST the most recent move toward your side mechanically raises CLV; (2) log Pinnacle/originator moves that follower books (DK etc.) haven't matched — the lag is a computable entry signal; (3) QB-out news is the largest single repricing in NFL (3-7 points), and betting the repriced side between credible practice-report news and the market's full move is the most reliable CLV-beat trigger available to a paper book restricted to real captured prices. Also record best-available price across books at capture — cross-book dispersion alone produced bootstrap-significant NFL returns.
survived.evidence: Simon (IJSF 2025 + Management Science 2024) found statistically significant negative autocorrelation in NFL/NBA/NHL moneyline moves across three books, with weak-form efficiency formally rejected in the companion MLB study; forecast accuracy does not even improve monotonically toward kickoff. Getty et al. (arXiv 1910.08858) showed line shopping across 16 books yielded NFL ROI with a 99% bootstrap CI of +8.11% to +82.85%, attributed to price dispersion, not prediction. Boyd's Bets position-value tiers (elite QB 5-7 pts, verified 2019 Brees case: 4-pt move) give the repricing magnitudes; Unabated's market-structure account (Pinnacle/CRIS originate, retail follows) matches Buchdahl's sharp-vs-soft asymmetry empirically.
survived.first_step: The Odds API capture job already needed for entry prices should poll multiple timestamps per game and store per-book prices + timestamps; add two derived fields at entry time — direction of the last line move at the benchmark book, and originator-vs-follower disagreement — then measure CLV beat rate conditional on each during the 9/3-5 rehearsal.

verdict.reasoning: Attempted refutation failed on the core claims. (1) The negative-autocorrelation citation is real and precise: Simon (2025), International Journal of Sport Finance, "Autocorrelation and Weekend Effects: Inefficiencies in Moneyline Movement for Three Major Sports" — NFL/NBA/NHL moneyline changes at three sportsbooks 2019-2023 show significant negative autocorrelation, framed as sportsbook overreaction; corroborated by "Inefficient Forecasts at the Sportsbook" (2023). Given negative autocorrelation, entering against the most recent move mechanically raises expected CLV vs the close. Moskowitz (JF 2021) momentum is in team-performance signals, not tick autocorrelation, so it does not contradict this. (2) Originator-vs-follower lag (Pinnacle/CRIS -> retail) is among the best-documented profitable timing strategies (steam chasing); books limit practitioners because it works, and those limits don't bind a paper book. (3) QB-out repricing of 3-7 points is confirmed nearly verbatim by multiple sources and is the largest single-news NFL repricing; the practice-report drift window is real, though official OUT designations reprice in seconds. (4) The one flaw: "cross-book dispersion alone produced bootstrap-significant NFL returns" misattributes the Kaunitz/Zhong/Kreiner (2017) bootstrap result (3.5% ROI, 10.8 sigma), which was European soccer, not NFL; no NFL-specific bootstrap-dispersion study found. The attached practice (record best-available price at capture) remains independently supported (line shopping ~1-3% ROI). Three of four load-bearing pillars independently confirmed, the mechanism is coherent, nothing is outdated or arbed-away for a paper book — so the claim as a whole stands, with the caveat that the final sentence's NFL attribution should read soccer-evidence-generalized. Sources: doi.org/10.1177/15586235251394815 (Simon 2025); researchgate.net/publication/372441761 (Inefficient Forecasts at the Sportsbook); Moskowitz JF 2021 (ssrn 2635517); arxiv.org/pdf/1710.02824 (Kaunitz et al., soccer); sportsinsights.com and boydsbets.com (steam/top-down); packernet.com and walterfootball.com (QB 3-7 point moves).

survived.title: Rebuild the props layer as deterministic distributions anchored on ffopportunity expected stats, with an injury kill rule and release-window entries
survived.claim: Fix the layer that produced 47/54 dead props: (a) price P(over) in code — Poisson for receptions, compound Poisson×Gamma for receiving yards, negative binomial where over-dispersed — anchored on ffopportunity's precomputed weekly expected stats (xReceptions, xRecYards, xRushYards from xgboost on nflverse pbp, downloadable per week back to 2006, zero leakage if served weeks < N), with Sonnet adjudicating only the news/context layer on top; (b) hard kill rule: no prop on a player with DNP/Limited Friday practice status (nflverse load_injuries(), timestamped, joins on existing keys with zero new infrastructure); (c) capture prop entries at line release (Tue-Wed), because prop lines are moved by sharps within ~30 seconds of release and closing-line prop grading structurally mismeasures the edge; (d) check the documented under bias replicates in the walk before promoting it — season-long prop unders hit 66.6% in two independent samples.
survived.evidence: OpticOdds documents the parametric-screen-then-simulate production pattern and warns plain Poisson is wrong for rushing-style props; the Poisson GLM reception model gives a concrete functional form. ETR's publicly graded record — profitable all 7 NFL seasons 2019-2025, 0.48% to 22.1% ROI on ~20 plays/week — proves projection-vs-line prop process works AND calibrates expectations (5-15% ROI typical, near-zero years happen, pass on most of the board). ETR's own FAQ documents the 30-second release-window reality; 4for4 independently found 10-15% cross-book prop price divergence and 66.6% under rate on 243 season-long props (Yahoo: +$6,800 at $100/bet, all six categories ≥55.6% under).
survived.first_step: Pull ffopportunity's precomputed weekly parquet for 2019-2024, wire a Poisson receptions pricer for one prop type, and grade it across the walk against realized results (not CLV) — then add the Friday practice-status kill rule from load_injuries() and count how many of the 47 dead props it would have blocked.

verdict.reasoning: Every load-bearing factual assertion survived refutation attempts via independent sources. (a) ffopportunity is real: xgboost trained on nflverse pbp 2006-2020, precomputed weekly releases with receptions_exp/rec_yards_gained_exp/rush_yards_gained_exp fields, loadable via load_ff_opportunity(); zero-leakage holds for post-2020 serving (only caveat: 2006-2020 weeks are in-sample to the model). (b) nflreadr load_injuries() confirmed with practice_status, report_status, and date_modified timestamp, data since 2009, standard gsis_id/season/week keys. (c) Independent expert consensus (Unabated and others) confirms prop CLV is structurally unreliable — few market-making books, low limits, no real price discovery — supporting release-window entry grading; the '~30 seconds' figure is anecdotal precision but the mechanism is consensus. (d) The season-long under bias is documented in multiple independent samples, including exact 66.6% (INT unders) and 66.1% (RB TD unders) figures plus a 1,392-prop 5-year dataset showing unders profitable 5 straight seasons; the claim correctly demands replication before promotion since the documented bias is season-long, not weekly. Minor quibbles (colloquial field names, anecdotal 30-second precision, in-sample training-window overlap, Friday-status-after-Tuesday-entry ordering) do not refute the claim's substance.

survived.title: Fix the devig itself: odds-weighted margin models (power/Shin), never naive proportional splitting — and re-grade the underdog doctrine under both schemes
survived.claim: If the quant fair-value model or the grader devigs by uniform proportional normalization, part of the measured +20% underdog edge is a devig artifact: naive margin splitting leaves ~0.5-0.6% systematic phantom value concentrated exactly on longshots/dogs. Implement power and Shin (or the closed-form odds-weighted formula: Fair Odds = n×BookOdds/(n − Margin×BookOdds)), and for moneyline dogs and prop alt-lines require the edge to survive the WORST-case fair value across methods before a pick boards — a frozen deterministic gate. Near -110 spreads the methods converge, so spend no effort there.
survived.evidence: Buchdahl's yield-to-zero test on 410,628 Pinnacle closing odds: blind betting at equal-margin 'fair' odds returned -0.56% (should be 0%), vs +0.10/-0.20/+0.07% for the three odds-weighted models, with 3,957 phantom 'value' longshots flagged only by the naive model. The 90,014-match arXiv study (2012-2024, five books) confirms Shin/power beat multiplicative at scale and estimates favorite-longshot bias beta 1.06-1.15 at EVERY bookmaker — longshots are systematically shaded against bettors, which is a direct caution on the dog doctrine. penaltyblog's scored comparison shows convergence at efficient short prices (0.19724 vs 0.19730 RPS); Outlier documents the additive-devig negative-probability hazard and ships worst-case mode as the conservative envelope.
survived.first_step: Swap the CLV-pivot's devig function to compute multiplicative, power, and Shin fair values side by side, then re-grade the 2019-2024 underdog-ATS ROI under naive vs odds-weighted devig and report the delta as a robustness line in the 8/17 validation.

verdict.reasoning: Attempted refutation failed on every load-bearing element. (1) Direction: independent literature (Shin 1992/93, Buchdahl's Wisdom of the Crowd, CRAN `implied` package docs) confirms bookmakers load margin disproportionately onto longshots, so naive proportional normalization overstates dog fair probability — phantom value concentrated exactly on dogs/longshots, as claimed; the `implied` vignette calls the basic proportional method the least accurate available. (2) Formula: the claim's closed-form Fair Odds = n·BookOdds/(n − Margin·BookOdds) is exactly the inverse of the documented margin-weights-proportional-to-odds method pi = (n − M·Oi)/(n·Oi) from Buchdahl — not invented. (3) Magnitude: a documented 1.25/4.20 example shows ~1.05pp dog-probability distortion (multiplicative 22.93% vs power 21.88%) at ~4.7% overround; scaled to sharp-book 2-3% margins this is ~0.4-0.6pp, matching the claimed ~0.5-0.6%. (4) Convergence at -110/-110 is mathematically true by symmetry and independently stated in devig references. (5) The worst-case-across-methods gate is a conservative, purely deterministic prescription that can only suppress picks, and the claim is properly conditional on the codebase actually using proportional devig. Methods are current, not outdated or arbed-away — they concern probability estimation, not an exploitable market inefficiency. No basis to refute.

survived.title: Doctrine hygiene: era-gate every lesson, localize edges by odds bin and home/road split, and grade doctrine against external frozen anchors
survived.claim: Add three deterministic disciplines to distillation: (1) era-validity — any totals/behavioral-bias lesson must survive on the most recent 3 seasons alone, because books switched to unbiased pricing ~2010 and famous biases flipped sign while bettor behavior stayed constant; (2) localization — adopt the alpha-by-implied-probability-bin table (Holm-Bonferroni corrected) as a standing grading report, and split the underdog doctrine home/road and by spread size: the literature's surviving bias story (road favorites overbet) predicts HOME dogs specifically, and if the edge doesn't concentrate where the mechanism predicts, it's noise; (3) external anchors — grade the '+1-to-+3 days rest sweet spot' against the peer-reviewed finding that post-2011-CBA rest effects are <0.5 pts and the market OVERprices byes (+0.97 priced vs +0.31 real), rather than letting the loop re-derive rest doctrine from its own picks. Also re-bucket wind as <15/15-20/20+ mph — a 'leak' in the sub-15 bucket is an overfitting red flag, since the physical effect has a ~15 mph knee and main weather effects are priced; the residual weather opportunity is derived markets (FG props, team totals) where the book's adjustment is a blunt game-total haircut.
survived.evidence: Kelly & Chen (4,600 games, 2001-2018): the ≥47.5 under bias went 59.7% (p=0.014) in 2001-2009 to 47.1% in 2010-2018 while the over-betting bias persisted at 64% and strengthened — proof that bias stories cannot justify totals lessons post-2010. Qureshi & Zaman's per-bin alpha diagnostic localized a real NBA edge to one odds bin (153 games, MW p=0.0003) while showing NFL ML stayed efficient even through COVID. The Frontiers Bayesian state-space study (5,679 games, 2002-2023, fit jointly to margins and spreads) gives the rest-market mispricing signs, including the one pro-rested residual: mini-bye (+0.48 real vs -0.06 priced). Sharp Football Analysis documents the 15/20 mph non-linearity and states main effects are priced.
survived.first_step: Add two fields to every doctrine entry — 'era_valid_recent3' (boolean, recomputed on the last 3 seasons only) and 'mechanism_localized' (the odds bin / home-road cell where the edge concentrates) — and run the alpha-by-bin table over the existing 2019-2024 graded picks this week, before the 2025 holdout.

verdict.reasoning: Attempted refutation failed on every falsifiable anchor. (1) Era-gating: AABRI totals-market study documents the exact ~2010 regime change — the contrarian under-on-high-totals bias strategy was profitable 2001-2009 and turned negative 2010-2018 (sign flip), consistent with books moving to less-biased pricing; Levitt (2004) documents the earlier bias-shading regime. (2) Localization: the literature says bettors overbet road favorites and large favorites, with the profitable counterpart being home underdogs (large home dogs ~59.7% ATS historically), so the claim's mechanism-predicts-home-dogs test is exactly what published research implies; Holm-Bonferroni binning is standard methodology. (3) Rest anchor: Lopez & Bliss 2024 (arXiv 2408.10867, Frontiers Behav. Econ., NFL League Office data) reports bye advantage +2.2 pts pre-2011 CBA falling to ~+0.3 after, while markets raised implied bye pricing from +0.39 to +0.97 pts — the claim's +0.97 priced vs +0.31 real and <0.5 pt figures are a near-exact citation of this peer-reviewed finding. (4) Wind: 15 mph is the standard impact threshold in wind analyses and sources note windy-game under edges dried up as markets adjusted, supporting 'main weather effects are priced' and the sub-15-leak-is-a-red-flag heuristic; the derived-markets clause is a prescription, uncontradicted. All specific checkable numbers matched independent published research, so the claim is supported, not refuted.

debunked: High-total unders (>=47.5): won 59.7% in 2001-2009, went 47.1% (245-218, -$4,350) in 2010-2018; re-anchoring to >=51.5 also loses (48.5%). The bettor over-bias persists but books stopped shading — the edge is structurally dead, not cyclical (Kelly & Chen, 4,600 games).

NFL moneyline inefficiency: none found even under the COVID no-fans regime shock (KS p=1.00 across 3,740 games 2007-2021) while the same test found +16.7% ROI in the NBA bubble. Confirms 'ML win% is a juice mirage' — drop ML from the market-selection set entirely.

Home-underdog / contrarian-dog ATS systems at closing lines: profitable pre-2005, gone by 2005-2011 (Humphreys, Paul & Weinbach 2013); the decay mechanism (competition forcing unbiased prices) is structural and one-directional. Treat the lab's +20% dog-ATS ROI as closing-line leakage until re-proven at entry prices.

Bye-week rest advantage: collapsed from +2.21 pts/game (2002-2010) to +0.31 non-significant post-2011 CBA, while the market still prices +0.97 — the market now OVERpays the bye team, and even fading it wins only ~52% (not enough vs vig). The current '+1-to-+3 days rest sweet spot' doctrine must survive this external anchor.

West-coast-team-travels-east fade: 82-86 ATS 2003-2016, and 25-15 ATS the OTHER way from 2013+ — the classic travel-fatigue edge is dead/reversed. Only the circadian night-game effect (66% ATS, 1970-2011 sample) is a candidate, and it needs post-2015 revalidation at a shrunken effect size.

Mild-weather / sub-15mph wind signals: physically the effect has a ~15 mph knee, so a 'leak' below 15 mph is an overfitting red flag, and main weather effects on totals are already priced. The current mild-weather/breezy doctrine bucket should be treated as suspect, not promoted.

Referee crew ATS/OU records: career marks like 57-56-1 and 65-47 are coin flips; the one outlier (Hussey 62.7% home ATS) is selection noise. Only the penalty-rate channel (8-10 penalties/game spread between crews, automatic-first-down rates) is a legitimate feature.

Same-game parlays as an edge source: leg correlation is already in the price at 15-25% hold vs 4-5% on singles; 'obviously correlated' stacks are not free EV. Paper SGPs are a hold-measurement instrument only.

Raw backtest win rates and raw Kelly: an NBA system at 56.0% over 484 bets went 4-8-2 out of sample; raw Kelly had ~38% ruin-halving probability vs ~0% for shrunken Kelly. Never size or trust an angle on its raw historical rate.

85-95% 'NFL prediction accuracy' claims in the academic ML literature: retrodictive (same-season inputs, points scored/allowed carry 88% of SHAP importance) — explanation, not forecast. Classify any surfaced 'X% accurate model' as non-bettable unless scored on future games at real prices.

CLV as a universal grader: meaningless in player props and other low-limit markets (the close is not sharpened), and raw line-vs-line CLV overstates edge 3-4x without devigging; consensus-average closes as benchmark predict nothing (only sharp-book closes predict realized returns).

Naive proportional devig: leaves ~0.5-0.6% phantom value concentrated on longshots (3,957 false 'value' longshots in Buchdahl's sample) — a direct contamination channel for any underdog doctrine measured through it. Additive devig can emit negative probabilities on longshots.

Bigger/pricier LLMs or deeper narrative analysis for pick quality: in the only public live LLM-bettor benchmark, the cheapest model beat Claude, one model blew its bankroll day one, and the winning behavior was explicit EV/Kelly math in code — never let the LLM size bets, and A/B any model upgrade against the frozen graded record.
